title: Why do sea breezes blow by day and land breezes at night?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why is it windy at the beach in the afternoon?
Why does the wind change direction at night by the sea?
Why does land heat up faster than water?

explain.say: Spend a sunny day at the beach and you often feel a cool breeze blowing in from the sea in the afternoon. At night it can turn around and blow out to sea.

explain.say: Land heats up much faster than water. By day the air over the hot land rises, and cooler, denser air from over the sea flows in to replace it: a sea breeze.

draw.verdict: Wind flows from the cooler side to the warmer

right.title: Night: land breeze
points: Air over the sea is warmer

explain.say: At night the land also cools faster than the water. Now the sea is the warmer side, air rises over it, and cool air flows from the land out to sea: a land breeze.

explain.say: This is the rule behind all winds, air flowing from cooler, higher pressure to warmer, lower pressure, on a small daily scale. A monsoon is the same idea on a giant, seasonal scale.

faq.q: Why does land heat up faster than the sea?
faq.a: Water needs far more energy to warm up than rock or soil, and sunlight spreads down into water while waves mix the heat around. Land heats only a thin top layer, so it warms and cools quickly.
asks: Why is the sea colder than the sand?

faq.a: A sea breeze is a cool wind that blows from the sea onto the land on sunny days, because air over the hot land rises and sea air flows in to take its place.
asks: Why is it windy at the beach?

faq.a: A land breeze blows from the land out to sea at night, when the land has cooled below the temperature of the sea.
asks: Why does the wind change at night by the sea?

faq.q: How far inland does a sea breeze reach?
faq.a: Usually a few tens of kilometres, though strong sea breezes can push much further inland. They are strongest on hot, sunny afternoons.
asks: How strong is a sea breeze?

faq.a: Yes. Large lakes make lake breezes in the same way, cooling the shore on hot afternoons.

facts: Water needs about five times as much energy as dry sand to warm by the same amount.
Sea breezes from both coasts of Florida often meet over the middle of the state and set off afternoon thunderstorms.
